claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the initial questions.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**To determine your eligibility, I need to understand your situation:**

First, could you tell me:
1. **How many children are you asking about?**
2. **What are their names and ages?**

This will help me understand which category they fall into and guide you through the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 18 years old and lives at home with you**.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For young people in this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in qualifying education or training.

Let me ask you some questions about Alex:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following:**
1. Full-time education (such as school, college, or university)
2. An approved training course (such as an apprenticeship)
3. Part-time education/training while also working

Could you let me know what Alex's current situation is?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels. He's studying full-time there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's very helpful to know. Alex is in full-time education at college doing A-levels.

Now I need to check a few more things about Alex's situation to complete the eligibility assessment:

**1. Is Alex working at all?** (either full-time, part-time, or any paid work?)

**2. How old will Alex be when he finishes his A-levels or leaves college?** (This helps me understand if there are any breaks in his education that might affect eligibility)

**3. Do you receive any Child Benefit or other benefits for Alex currently, or has this been assessed before?**

These details will help me determine Alex's full eligibility status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. No, Alex isn't working at all - he's just focused on his studies right now.

2. He should finish when he's 19, assuming everything goes to plan with his exams.

3. No, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him - that's why I'm checking if I can claim it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details! That's very helpful. Let me navigate through the assessment based on Alex's situation.

Since Alex is 18, in full-time education at college, and not working, let me check the next part of the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect. Now let me move forward - since Alex is currently in full-time education at college:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! This is excellent news for Alex. He's studying A-levels, which is **approved non-advanced education**. A-levels are specifically listed as qualifying education.

Now I need to check one more important criterion - whether Alex is working full-time (which would disqualify him). You mentioned he's not working at all, so let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not working at all, he definitely meets this requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right**, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (for himself, not as a dependent)

You mentioned you're not currently receiving Child Benefit for him, but I need to check if Alex has any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh yes, actually Alex does receive Universal Credit in his own name. He applied for it himself to help with his costs while studying.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I understand - Alex has applied for and is receiving Universal Credit in his own name.

Unfortunately, this means **Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit**. According to the eligibility rules, children who are receiving certain benefits in their own right - including Universal Credit - do not qualify for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm the outcome formally:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

**Alex - NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Why:** While Alex meets most of the requirements for Child Benefit (he's 18, in full-time approved education doing A-levels, and not working full-time), he is disqualified because he is receiving Universal Credit in his own name.

**What this means:**
- You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex
- This is because the rules state that children receiving certain benefits in their own right are not eligible for Child Benefit
- This applies specifically to Universal Credit and Employment and Support Allowance

**Advice:**
If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops receiving Universal Credit), you could potentially reapply for Child Benefit at that point. However, while he's receiving UC, he remains ineligible.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or are there any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?
